_comment: Stage 1 of tests/journeys/subscription-lifecycle.spec.js. Accounts and products are pre-existing org sample data: resolved by name, never created, never swept. setQuantityInUi drives both the QLE edit steps and the API quantity assertions, so a quantity is stated in exactly one place. No expectedNetTotal anywhere by design: correctness is asserted on the data model, not on formatted currency.
_bundles: Every product listed here must be a SIMPLE product. Selecting a bundle navigates to the product configurator instead of returning to the selection screen, which strands this flow. 'Home Security Console' was removed for that reason; bundle configuration lives in tests/config/solar-bundle-configuration.spec.js, which drives the configurator deliberately via ProductSelectionPage.selectBundle() and data/solar-bundle.json.
_productCode: productCode is what identifies a row in the Product Selection grid — the name is not unique enough. Searching 'Warranty' returns LDWARRANTY (Loss and Damage Warranty), WARRANTY and WARRANTYEXTENSION, and a name-substring match would take the first. The grid renders the code as the first column, so the code is matched exactly against it.
_pricebook: An Opportunity created over the REST API gets NO price book (the UI assigns one). Without Pricebook2Id, Salesforce cannot create Opportunity Products at all, so marking the quote Primary silently produces zero of them and leaves Opportunity.Amount null. The Id lives here rather than in code because it is org-specific, and no record Id belongs in a spec. Leave pricebookId null to fall back to resolving the org's active standard price book by query.

opportunity.baseName: Home security system with exterior cameras

_expected: Stages 2-4. Every value here is a RECORD-level outcome CPQ produces in response to a UI action — no formatted currency, no rendered strings. Stated exactly once each: the spec derives nothing it could instead read from here, and duplicates nothing it reads.

expected._orderCount: Checking Ordered on a primary quote with SBQQ__OrderByQuoteLineGroup__c = true splits it into one Order per quote line group. Two groups, two Orders — the whole point of stage 2. A quote WITHOUT that flag produces one Order instead, which is why stage 2 re-checks the flag before it counts anything.
expected._ordersByGroup: Order Products (OrderItem) expected on the Order generated from each group — one per quote line in that group. Keyed by group name, matching the `groups` array above.
expected._subscriptionCount: SBQQ__Subscription__c records under the Contract that contracting the Ongoing Services order generates — one per subscription-priced quote line in that group.
expected._assetCount: Assets generated by contracting the One-time Purchases order. NOT one per line: the count follows each product's SBQQ__AssetConversion__c, which is why assetsByProduct below is asserted per product rather than inferred from this total. 3 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 5.
expected._assetsByProduct: assetConversion values were READ FROM THE ORG on 2026-07-27 (SOQL on Product2.SBQQ__AssetConversion__c in the Developer org), not guessed — the rule in README Section 10 forbids a plausible-looking guess, not a verified value. Re-confirm if the catalog changes. 'One per unit' multiplies by the quote line quantity; 'One per quote line' yields exactly one regardless of quantity; null means no asset conversion and yields none at all.

Home Security Installation._note: no asset conversion set on the product — asserted explicitly, never inferred from the total

_amendmentRenewal: Stages 5-7 of the subscription journey (tests/journeys/subscription-renewal.spec.js): renewal forecast, two contract amendments, renewal quote. Same rules as `expected` above — every value is a RECORD-level outcome, never a formatted string. Nothing here is seeded; every record these stages assert against is one CPQ produced in response to a UI action.

amendmentRenewal._org: Org configuration these stages DEPEND ON but never create. Both were read from the Developer org on 2026-07-28 and are asserted at the top of stage 5, so a missing one fails by name instead of surfacing later as 'Warranty is still on the renewal opportunity', which reads like a CPQ defect.

renewalSubstitution._setupPath: Setup -> Products -> Warranty -> Renewal Product = Warranty Extension (Product2.SBQQ__RenewalProduct__c)
renewalSubstitution._confirmed: 2026-07-28, Developer org: Product2 WARRANTY has SBQQ__RenewalProduct__c -> Warranty Extension.
renewalSubstitution._theRule: A renewal forecast prices its lines TWO different ways, and the discriminator is SUBSTITUTION. A carried-forward line keeps the predecessor subscription's pricing, pro-rated to the renewal term. A SUBSTITUTED successor has no predecessor price to carry — it is a different product — so it takes its OWN PricebookEntry.UnitPrice, 15 for Warranty Extension. Warranty is the only substituted line on this opportunity, which is why it is the only one that does not follow the pro-ration. Every expected number now lives in renewalForecast.expectedUnitPrices, stated once, and the spec asserts BOTH the literal and the model that produces it.
renewalSubstitution._previousReading: READ ON 2026-07-28 (Developer org, contract 00000109): 10.00 on the Warranty Extension renewal line, and read as the predecessor's price carried forward — Warranty's subscription nets 20.00 over the 24-month contract, so 20 x 12/24 = 10. That reading was UNFALSIFIABLE at the time: Warranty's carried-forward price and Warranty Extension's own list price were both 10 as far as that one line could show, and only the fact that the successor's PricebookEntry is 15 (unchanged since 2025-01-14) separates them. Kept because it explains why the substitution rule was not visible from a single line, which is what the all-four assertion now fixes.
renewalSubstitution._whyTheOldReadingWas10: Every 10.00 reading in this org predates 2026-08-01 and every 15.00 reading follows it. Measured: contracts 00000112, 00000113 and 00000114 (runs of 2026-07-30 and 07-31) all show 10 on the successor line; contracts 00000115, 00000116 and 00000117 (2026-08-01 onward, the last being the run that verified these assertions) all show 15, at forecast time AND after both amendments. Product2 WARRANTYEXTENSION was last modified 2026-08-01T08:59:40Z and now carries SBQQ__PricingMethod__c = 'Percent Of Total'. The correlation is exact and the timestamp is recorded here, but the MECHANISM is not proven and is deliberately not claimed — what is asserted is the behaviour, which has been stable across three consecutive runs.
renewalSubstitution._theProrationBase: The carried-forward derivation the spec computes is subscription SBQQ__NetPrice__c x renewalTerm / Contract.ContractTerm. That is only 'pro-rate to the renewal term' because every subscription on the contract AT STAGE 5 spans the contract's full term — they all come from the one original order. Amendment subscriptions do NOT: measured on contract 00000117, the Mobile Control Center App row added by amendment 2 spans 12 months, not 24, and its renewal line follows ITS term rather than the contract's. Stage 5 runs before any amendment, so the formula holds there. Nothing silently relies on it either way: the literals in expectedUnitPrices are asserted alongside the derivation, so a changed base disagrees with a pinned number rather than sliding past.

replacementProduct.name: Mobile Control Center App
replacementProduct._setupPath: Setup -> Products -> Mobile Control Center App, and a PricebookEntry in the Opportunity's price book (01sbm000007eqofAAA).
replacementProduct._confirmed: 2026-07-28, Developer org: simple product (SBQQ__ConfigurationType__c is null, so Add Products returns to the selection screen rather than opening the configurator), SBQQ__SubscriptionPricing__c = Fixed Price, PricebookEntry $5.00 in the Standard Price Book.

amendmentRenewal._stage5: Renewal forecast. Checking SBQQ__RenewalForecast__c on the activated Contract makes CPQ generate a renewal Opportunity carrying one OpportunityLineItem per subscription, with any product that has a Renewal Product substituted for its successor.

renewalForecast._renewalTerm: Months, written onto Contract.SBQQ__RenewalTerm__c. Deliberately 12 rather than the contract's own 24, so the assertion proves the field was set by this stage instead of matching a value that was already there — the Contract defaults SBQQ__RenewalTerm__c to its ContractTerm.
renewalForecast._opportunityBaseName: The runId is appended at runtime. A fixed name collides across runs; every downstream reference in stages 6 and 7 resolves by Id anyway, so the name is for a human opening the org.
renewalForecast._expectedLineCount: One OpportunityLineItem per subscription on the contract. Equal to expected.subscriptionCount above, and read from there rather than repeated — stated here only as a reminder of the relationship.
renewalForecast._productsAbsent: Asserted explicitly, by name. A line count that happens to match is a passing test that proves nothing about the substitution — the whole scenario is that Warranty left and Warranty Extension arrived.
renewalForecast._expectedUnitPrices: UnitPrice on EVERY renewal line, one entry per productsPresent, READ FROM THE ORG on 2026-08-02 off the two most recent pristine forecasts (renewal opportunities 006bm00000UTOYkAAP / contract 00000115 and 006bm00000UUeRlAAL / contract 00000116, both identical). Asserting all four rather than the successor alone is what separates the two pricing models: a failure on Warranty Extension ALONE means the substitution behaviour moved, a failure across the other three means the pro-ration did, and with one line asserted those two are the same red test. See org.renewalSubstitution._theRule.
renewalForecast._carriedForwardDerivation: The three carried-forward lines are the predecessor subscription's per-unit SBQQ__NetPrice__c scaled by renewalTerm / Contract.ContractTerm, i.e. x 12/24 here. Home Security Monitoring 400 -> 200, Mobile Monitoring App 48 -> 24, Offsite Video Storage 24 -> 12 (net price is PER UNIT, so the storage line's quantity of 2 does not enter into it). The spec derives that product-by-product from the contract's own subscriptions at run time and asserts it alongside the literals above — the literal catches a rule that stopped firing, the derivation catches one computing from the wrong base.
renewalForecast._mobileIsNot60: Mobile Monitoring App is 24 here, NOT the 60 an earlier note recorded. 60 was Mobile Control Center App, a DIFFERENT product that does not exist on this opportunity until amendment 2 replaces the Monitoring App in stage 6 — the two list at 2/month and 5/month respectively, so carrying 60 into stage 5 would assert the successor's price against the predecessor's line. And 60 is itself stale: MOBILECONTROLCENTER was switched to SBQQ__PricingMethod__c = 'Block' on 2026-08-01T06:17Z with a 1-5 tier at 3.00, so it now renews at 36 (3 x 12 months). Nothing in stage 5 touches it — recorded because the same note is what made 60 look like a stage 5 number.
renewalForecast._substitutedProduct: Not listed here. The spec derives it from org.renewalSubstitution.to.name and treats every other line as carried forward, so the substituted product is named in exactly one place.

amendmentRenewal._stage6: Two amendments against the same Contract. Both must roll into the EXISTING contract rather than spawning a new one, which is the scenario's headline claim and gets its own assertion.

amendments._startDateOffsetMonths: Months after the contract's own start date (ctx.startDate, the first of next year). Derived from that, never from new Date(): computing 'July 1st of next year' independently drifts if stage 1 ran on December 31.

quantityIncrease._quantity: The NEW TOTAL typed into the amendment quote's quantity cell. The contract already carries 2, so the delta is 3.
quantityIncrease._deltaQuantity: What the new SBQQ__Subscription__c line on the Contract should carry — the delta, not the new total. CPQ records an amendment as an additional subscription row for the increment.
quantityIncrease._quoteLineNetTotal: READ FROM THE ORG on 2026-07-28 (Developer org, contract 00000109, amendment quote Q-00144): SBQQ__NetTotal__c = 54 on the Offsite Video Storage amendment line. This IS the pro-ration, and it checks out arithmetically — see _netTotalDerivation. Not a guess, and not a value copied from a rendered string.
quantityIncrease._netTotalDerivation: 3 extra units x $1.00/month list x 18 months remaining = $54.00. The 18 months are from the amendment start date (2027-07-01) to the contract end (2028-12-31), which is exactly what pro-rating an amendment means — a full-term amount would be 3 x $1 x 24 = $72.
quantityIncrease._quantityFields: READ FROM THE ORG on 2026-07-28, same run. CPQ splits an amendment quantity across three fields: SBQQ__Quantity__c holds the NEW TOTAL (5), SBQQ__PriorQuantity__c holds what the contract already carried (2), and SBQQ__EffectiveQuantity__c holds the DELTA (3). All three are asserted in the spec, because the failure worth catching is CPQ moving the delta to a different field, not the number being off.

productReplacement._terminate: Quantity is set to 0 on the amendment quote line, which is how CPQ terminates a subscription. That produces a Contract subscription row with a NEGATIVE quantity, dated to the amendment start date.

amendments._expectedSubscriptionCount: READ FROM THE ORG on 2026-07-28 (Developer org, contract 00000109): 7 SBQQ__Subscription__c rows once both amendments are contracted. CPQ never edits an existing subscription row — it appends one per change, so the contract reads as a ledger: 4 original (2027-01-01) + 1 for the +3 Offsite Video Storage increment (2027-07-01) + 1 for the -1 Mobile Monitoring App termination (2028-01-01) + 1 for the Mobile Control Center App replacement (2028-01-01) = 7.

amendmentRenewal._stage7: Renewal quote. Checking SBQQ__RenewalQuoted__c generates a Quote against the renewal Opportunity holding only the subscription products — the one-time hardware from the other quote line group must not appear.

renewalQuote._productsPresent: The subscription products as they stand after both amendments: Warranty substituted for Warranty Extension by the renewal forecast, and Mobile Monitoring App replaced by Mobile Control Center App by the second amendment.
renewalQuote._productsAbsent: The one-time hardware went to a different Order and became Assets, never subscriptions, so none of it can legitimately reach a renewal quote. Asserted by NAME rather than by count — a total that happens to match proves nothing about which products are on it.
renewalQuote._quantities: Quantities that must carry through from an amendment. Offsite Video Storage went 2 -> 5 in the first amendment, so the renewal quote line has to reflect the amended total, not the original.
